subject: Excluding some rows from loaded data (Newbie)

messages.author: 770d8c26a9e58f60
messages.subject: Excluding some rows from loaded data (Newbie)
parts:
I have a table of number of "accidental deaths by natural causes" in India. It's in the following format:

Year, Cause, Number of Death

The list is clean, i.e. when I do summary(accidents) no NAs are shown and it's plotting okay. 

Then, I wanted to remove a particular cause, so I ran:
> accidents2 <- accidents[which (accidents$Cause !="Other natural causes"),]
> summary (accidents2) was okay, and it plotted alright

The, I wanted to remove one more cause, so I ran:
> accidents3 <- accidents2[which (accidents$Cause != "Earthquake/Landslide"),]
> summary(accidents3) is showing NA's: 8 and it's showing error when I try to plot it.

Question:
1. What went wrong in excluding the data the second time?
2. How do I know that only data that is removed is the one that I expected? (I wanted all rows with "Earthquake/Landslide" as a cause to not be there)
3. Are there any things that I should watch out for when excluding certain data? Is there a better way to exclude data?

Sorry, if the question is a bit lengthy or naive - am happy to receive URLs as answers. Thanks in advance.

- rg

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: Excluding some rows from loaded data (Newbie)
parts:
I would do something like

data(iris)
subset(iris, Species == "setosa")
subset(iris, Species == c("setosa", "virginica"))

General coding answers can be found on the r-help list and stackoverflow (among others).

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: 03ece3b1305af652
messages.subject: Re: Excluding some rows from loaded data (Newbie)
parts:
The size of your objects are different. I would think that if instead you did

accidents3 <- accidents2[which (accidents2$Cause != "Earthquake/Landslide"),]
summary(accidents3) is showing NA's: 8 and it's showing error when I try to plot it.

note that it's accidents2 in the which statement, instead of accidents. If your previous subset worked, the shape of accidents and accidents2 are different. You may have pulled out 8 id's from accidents that were beyond the number of rows of accidents2

Matthew
